overview: Black pushes ...h5 on move two, aiming for ...h4 to open the h-file against White's g3 set-up. White can simply play h4 to stop it or ignore it and develop normally with Bg2 and Nc3. Black weakens the kingside and gets a slightly odd position for it.

white_ideas.idea: Stop it with 3.h4 or ignore it and play Bg2
Develop with Nc3 and Nf3 and use g5 square
Exploit the weak g5 and h5 squares

typical_structures.structure: English with g3 against Black e5 and h5

character.notes: Flank-pawn oddity with little forcing play.

gambit.notes: No material is given up in the main line.

soundness.notes: Black wastes time and has weaknesses; a doubtful idea.

character.reason: Nothing forcing happens early and White just develops.

soundness.reason: Black spends a move on a weakening wing pawn push.

approach.reason: Strong players do not play ...h5 here.

level.reason: A doubtful line is not a beginner choice.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes against the weakened wing.
